title: Alberti fixed-index cipher: state changes carried by decoded numeral controls
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED, NOT SELECTED. A complete letter-stream channel is explicitly described in Alberti’s Latin cipher treatise, consulted in Meister1906 pp136-139 (Getty Research Institute digitization). Its alphabet alignment changes when a transmitted letter decodes to a numeral control under the old alignment. This is a real historical state-dependent mechanism, distinct from GDT604’s fixed U/P/S token attack. It supplies no Voynich key, language, message boundary or historical connection; the work is generally dated circa1466-1467, later than the usual manuscript-production hypothesis. No decoder or target data accessed.

design.mechanism: Use exactly the source’s basic fixed-outer-index letter mode, not its separate optional sentence codebook. Two matching24-position disks have an ordered outer ring of20 letters and digits1..4, and an inner ring containing24 distinct signs in an agreed mixed order. The outer letter index B is the source example. The first transmitted lower-case sign is placed under B to initialize. Subsequently decode at the current alignment. If the sign denotes an ordinary outer letter, output that letter and keep alignment. If it denotes one of the four digits, consume it as a control and rotate that very inner sign under B. The optional336-entry sentence codebook and optional capital-letter nulls are not invoked. Their use would require separately specified conventions; no combined parser is silently invented.
design.formalization: Let O be the fixed outer cyclic sequence, pi(c) the inner position of transmitted sign c, j=position_O(B), and s the alignment modulo24. For initial sign c0 set s=j-pi(c0), emit nothing. For each later c compute y=O[(pi(c)+s) mod24]. If y is a letter emit y and retain s; if y is a digit emit nothing and set s=j-pi(c). In the latter case delta_s=j-position_O(y) mod24, so only four transitions are available from a state. The encoder may choose when to insert these controls, but the recipient’s transition is determined by the received stream and fixed key. No arbitrary hidden-state transition matrix, per-word alphabet or guessed reset is allowed.
design.unit: The source describes complete correspondence with an initial alignment indicator. Any proposed target unit must therefore be an independently delimited whole message, not an assumed line or paragraph reset. Exact target atomic signs, the indicator/data convention, exterior alphabet transcription and treatment of word spaces must be fixed before an empirical contract; none is established. The original is a20-letter stream, not lossless full modern Latin spelling including every punctuation and alphabet distinction.
design.contrast: GDT603/604 model each whitespace token as one U or one P+S surface with fixed138-type capacities and state-specific homophone maps. Alberti’s decoded value depends on a persistent alignment shared across a stream, and the same written sign can be payload or control in different alignments. Thus604 does not exclude this mechanism. Conversely historical existence does not reopen604 or justify another language-model attack. GDT882’s small fixed source-letter morphism rank corollary cannot simply be applied to an alignment-dependent output code; no claim of target compatibility follows.
design.identifiability: Even with known message boundaries and the native24-symbol inventory, every inner permutation and chosen index deterministically decodes every syntactically valid sign stream. Basic syntactic acceptance therefore supplies no decipherment evidence. Rotating the whole inner ring is a pure parameter gauge. Remaining inequivalent inner orders generally produce different plaintexts and control locations. A short stream starting c0,c1 with c1 distinct can map its second sign to different ordinary letters under different admissible inner orders. Making control recognition state-dependent does not identify that state/key. Exact externally bound plaintext, independently identified indicators or another nonlinguistic message constraint would still be needed; no one-best LM output or fluent sentence resolves this.
design.prediction: Only after an independently justified complete-message domain and external binding exist could one freeze all keys and test exact whole held messages with their own source-prescribed initial indicator. Retain all surviving keys and report disagreements or absent symbol values as unknown. A held message cannot select the key or repair missing controls. No test or implementation is selected here.
design.source: Primary Latin edition: Aloys Meister, Die Geheimschrift im Dienste der paepstlichen Kurie, Paderborn1906, pp136-139, https://archive.org/details/diegeheimschrift00meis . Contributor: Getty Research Institute. Native printed pages136,137,138,139 inspected; the fixed-index method is p138. Source page URLs use archive page indices n151,n152,n153,n154 respectively; downloaded scandata leafNum is offset by one, so printed page numbers control citation. Relevant p138 image https://archive.org/download/diegeheimschrift00meis/page/n153/mode/1up SHA256 b8eb388ad36a36c42e49679110deed5443a25ca3da9e54cb31200359d989171f; p137 image https://archive.org/download/diegeheimschrift00meis/page/n152/mode/1up SHA256 dbefe3b26663e4e726b90e145be42582d12fb9cbc2dd0cb13220164482f94384. The editor records manuscript variants, including k/r index and K/D signal examples; one must not silently fuse them. The algorithm uses the unambiguous fixed-B passage. This is an edition of the original Latin, not merely a modern cipher-disk reconstruction.
design.dating: Institutional contextual descriptions date De cifris to1466 or1467: Harvard Library Bulletin article https://dash.harvard.edu/server/api/core/bitstreams/d34aa5b4-1056-4f21-aa1c-141ba502e469/content and Trinity College https://www.cs.trincoll.edu/~crypto/historical/alberti.html . Dates in older institutional cryptographic retrospectives vary around1470. The native page inspected does not itself establish a composition date. No early-fifteenth-century attestation of this exact channel or connection to Voynich has been shown. The first Italian publication is1568; its text was not used to fill gaps in the Latin.
design.scope: Bounded source/mathematical finding only. Route-check and bounded ideas search/duplicates preceded source work; GDT603 REPORT and GDT604 METHOD were read. No target transcription, target image, sealed data, decoder, corpus, LM training, synthetic key search or new experiment. No parameter caps or alternative channel invented to rescue earlier failures. Earlier incidental public-target exposure remains relevant to future blinding assignments.
